title: Generalist and ambient agents consume evidence, publish via Fabric
statement: Foundation/generalist and ambient agents consume Knowledge Catalog / Spanner Graph / BigQuery evidence and publish research tasks and results through the Fabric as typed events.
rationale: Agents that read and write outside the Fabric produce research nobody can replay or attribute.

sources.section: §11 Cognitive, Model and Quantum Compute Plane

verification.check: An agent run reads evidence through a store adapter and its research task appears as a typed Fabric/event-log record; deleting the publish call makes the test fail.

notes: GCP placement column names Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform or GKE for persistent agents; GKE conflicts with ADR 0024 (Cloud Run + one Compute Engine node per region, no Kubernetes for workloads).

title: Custom model training on GPU/TPU/CPU producing versioned artifacts
statement: Custom model training runs as Vertex custom training/pipelines on GPU/TPU/CPU, reading training datasets from GCS/BigQuery/Bigtable snapshots, and outputs versioned model artifacts.
rationale: Training from live mutable stores cannot be reproduced; unversioned artifacts cannot be rolled back.

sources.section: §11 Cognitive, Model and Quantum Compute Plane

verification.check: A training job is submitted from a snapshot reference and the produced artifact carries a version and the snapshot digest; removing the snapshot reference fails the test.

title: Model registry records versions, evaluation, lineage, aliases, promotion evidence
statement: A model registry holds every model version with its evaluation, lineage, aliases and the evidence that justified its promotion.
rationale: A model that cannot be traced to its evaluation and promotion evidence cannot be audited or safely rolled back.

sources.section: §11 Cognitive, Model and Quantum Compute Plane

verification.check: Registering, evaluating and promoting a model leaves version, evaluation, lineage, alias and promotion evidence readable; removing the evaluation makes require_for_decision refuse.

notes: Text places it on Vertex Model Registry / ML metadata; the in-tree registry is a Rust equivalent.

title: World-model federation maintains competing scored models; disagreement is research signal
statement: Multiple competing world models/graphs are maintained and scored, and their disagreement is recorded and turned into a research signal rather than averaged away.
rationale: A single shared world model cannot say the models disagree; an average hides that the platform does not know.

sources.section: §11 Cognitive, Model and Quantum Compute Plane

verification.check: Two registered models that disagree produce an Arbitration carrying the Disagreement and a ResearchTask in the cycle's journal; collapsing to a mean fails the test.

notes: Placement: Spanner Graph + GKE/agent workers.

title: Symbolic reasoners produce machine-checkable proofs or constraints
statement: Symbolic/neuro-symbolic reasoning runs on dedicated compute and produces machine-checkable proofs or constraint results wherever possible.
rationale: A conclusion that cannot be checked mechanically can only be trusted, not verified.

sources.section: §11 Cognitive, Model and Quantum Compute Plane

verification.check: A reasoning outcome carries a checkable constraint/proof artefact that an independent checker re-verifies; corrupting the artefact fails verification.

notes: Names Z3/OR-Tools/Python reasoners: conflicts with ADR 0002/0009 (serde/serde_json only) and ADR 0001 (Rust everywhere).

title: Simulation covers replay, no-action branches, interventions, strategy validation
statement: The simulation/counterfactual capability provides market replay, no-action branches, intervention simulation and strategy validation over retained history.
rationale: Without a no-action branch every intervention looks causal; without replay a strategy cannot be validated.

sources.section: §11 Cognitive, Model and Quantum Compute Plane

verification.check: A replay of retained history yields the same decisions; an intervention candidate set without a no-action baseline is refused.

notes: Placement: GKE Jobs + batch compute; BigQuery/GCS history.

title: Quantum admits only asynchronous eligible research job classes
statement: The quantum path admits only asynchronous jobs of the eligible classes (optimisation, search, QML research) through a controlled egress gateway to IBM Quantum.
rationale: A synchronous quantum call would make execution depend on an external queue the platform does not control.

sources.section: §11 Cognitive, Model and Quantum Compute Plane

verification.check: admit_job refuses a synchronous job and any class outside the eligible set, and the production submission path calls it; removing the call from the path fails an integration test.

title: Classical benchmark and validation gate any quantum artifact promotion
statement: No quantum-produced artifact may be promoted unless a classical benchmark was computed on the same problem and the result validated against it.
rationale: "We used a quantum computer" is not a result; an unvalidated quantum answer could reach a decision.

sources.section: §11 Cognitive, Model and Quantum Compute Plane

verification.check: Each routing decision carries a finite classical objective; a quantum-gateway artifact is refused at promotion and a quantum-informed one is admitted only with its calibrated baseline. Deleting the classical solve or the refusal fails the tests.

title: Large-model outputs distilled into bounded compact Reflex models and signed bundles
statement: Large model outputs are distilled/compiled into bounded compact Reflex models and signed policy bundles through a training pipeline.
rationale: A Reflex node cannot evaluate a large model inside its latency budget, and an unsigned bundle can be swapped.

sources.section: §11 Cognitive, Model and Quantum Compute Plane

verification.check: A distilled student carries a bounded worst-case cost and its digest appears in a signed manifest the cell verifies; altering a coefficient changes the digest and the cell refuses it.

title: Reflex Node never calls a general model endpoint for a live order
statement: A Reflex Node never calls a general model endpoint to decide an order.
rationale: A remote model on the order path makes execution depend on a non-deterministic, slow, external service.

verification.check: The dependency graph shows no edge crate or edge-node reaching the language-model/AI crates; adding such an edge fails the architecture suite.

notes: Text says 'live order'; the platform is paper-only (ADR 0003), so the invariant is applied to every order the cell decides.

title: Reflex executes only locally loaded, tested, signed packages with deterministic risk
statement: A Reflex Node executes only a locally loaded, tested, signed model/policy package, with deterministic risk checks.
rationale: An unsigned or untested package on the order path is an unreviewed change to trading behaviour.

verification.check: The cell refuses a policy whose signature fails and a model its manifest does not name; risk gates are deterministic. Mutating the signature check fails the test.

title: Intelligence decomposed into independently scalable services
statement: The intelligence platform is decomposed into independently scalable services rather than one global model endpoint.
rationale: One global endpoint is a single point of failure and cannot scale workloads independently.

verification.check: Each named cognitive service is a separately deployable binary with its own scaling settings.

title: Cognitive services exchange typed Rust Fabric contracts and own narrow state
statement: Each cognitive service publishes/consumes typed Rust Fabric contracts and owns a narrow state domain.
rationale: Shared mutable state between services makes failures and changes non-local.

verification.check: Every cross-service message is a typed qip-contracts body with a schema-lock row; a service reading another's state directly fails the architecture suite.

title: Each cognitive service degrades without stopping local execution
statement: Every cognitive service can degrade or fail without stopping local (Reflex) execution.
rationale: If cognition is on the critical path, a research outage halts trading.

verification.check: With every central input stale/unavailable the cell still completes passes with reduced sizing; making a capability required for a pass fails the test.

title: Persistent cognitive services on regional GKE; burst on Vertex/accelerators
statement: Persistent cognitive services run primarily on regional/multi-region GKE Standard; burst training, evaluation and simulation use Vertex AI, GKE accelerator pools and batch compute.
rationale: Placement decision for warm cognition and burst compute.

verification.check: A plan shows the cognitive services on the stated runtime.

notes: Conflicts with ADR 0024 (Cloud Run + one Compute Engine node per region, no Kubernetes for workloads).

title: now-state-coordinator produces GlobalState, RegionalState, SurpriseEvent
statement: A now-state-coordinator consumes knowledge deltas, market state and model residuals and produces GlobalState, RegionalState and SurpriseEvent contracts.
rationale: Without one estimate of the present state, every consumer builds its own and they disagree.

verification.check: Feeding deltas and residuals produces typed GlobalState/RegionalState and a SurpriseEvent when a residual exceeds its bound.

title: NOW state partitioned by domain and region
statement: NOW state is partitioned by domain and region so it scales and fails per partition.
rationale: A single global state store is a single point of contention and failure.

verification.check: State keys carry domain and region; a write to one partition does not touch another.

title: Stale NOW state lowers confidence and never blocks Reflex
statement: Stale NOW state lowers confidence and never blocks Reflex execution.
rationale: A blocking dependency on central state turns a cognition outage into a trading outage.

verification.check: With NOW state past its freshness bound, confidence drops and the cell still runs; making the cell wait on NOW fails the test.

title: state-filter-workers produce latent-state candidates; missing worker reduces diversity
statement: State-filter workers turn typed observations and state priors into candidate latent-state updates, and a missing worker reduces ensemble diversity rather than failing estimation.
rationale: An estimator that fails when one ensemble member is missing is less available than any member.

verification.check: Removing one worker still yields an estimate with a reported smaller ensemble.

title: state-reconciler is a single fenced domain leader promoting state
statement: A state-reconciler, run as a single domain leader with fencing, promotes state and confidence from candidate states and symbolic constraints.
rationale: Two leaders promoting state concurrently produce two truths.

verification.check: A reconciler with a stale fencing epoch cannot promote; candidates violating a symbolic constraint are not promoted.

title: Last promoted state remains valid until expiry
statement: When the reconciler is unavailable, the last promoted state remains valid until its expiry.
rationale: Dropping state on a leader failure creates a gap; keeping it forever serves stale truth.

verification.check: After reconciler loss the state is served until expires_at and refused after.

title: forecast-router routes questions by domain/horizon/model society
statement: A forecast-router routes forecast questions by domain, horizon and model society using a routing/reputation cache, and falls back to default ensembles on failure.
rationale: Routing every question to one model ignores where each model is competent.

verification.check: A question is routed to the model with the best reputation in its context; with the cache unavailable the default ensemble answers.

title: forecast-micro runs calibrated microstructure forecasts locally
statement: Microsecond-to-minute calibrated microstructure forecasts run locally in Reflex (with warm backup) and continue independently of central services.
rationale: Remote microstructure forecasts arrive after the moment they forecast.

verification.check: The cell evaluates a local model in its pass with no network call; central unavailability does not stop it.

title: forecast-tactical outputs expire when stale and feed capital sizing
statement: Minutes-to-days tactical forecasts expire when stale, and capital sizing contracts on their staleness.
rationale: A stale forecast that keeps sizing positions is a decision on old information.

verification.check: A forecast past its expiry is not used and sizing shrinks; removing the expiry check fails the test.

title: forecast-strategic outage accumulates backlog, never an execution outage
statement: Weeks-to-years strategic forecasts run as a separate service whose outage only accumulates research backlog and never causes an execution outage.
rationale: Long-horizon research is not latency-critical and must not be able to stop trading.

verification.check: Stopping the strategic service leaves execution passing.

title: forecast-calibrator scores calibration, quantiles/intervals, regime scorecards
statement: A forecast-calibrator performs calibration, quantile/interval scoring and regime scorecards, keeping score history.
rationale: Uncalibrated forecasts make confidence arithmetic meaningless.

verification.check: Resolved forecasts produce Brier/interval scores by regime stored durably; removing the scoring call fails the test.

title: On calibrator failure, model influence freezes at last safe weights
statement: If the calibrator fails, model influence freezes at the last safe weights.
rationale: Weights updated from a broken calibrator drift arbitrarily.

verification.check: With calibration unavailable the weights equal the last safe set; mutating to keep updating fails.

title: Agents are not all required to use the same runtime
statement: The platform must not require every agent to use the same runtime; managed sessions/memory may use Agent Engine and long-lived deterministic agents run elsewhere.
rationale: Forcing one runtime either over-pays for simple agents or under-serves custom ones.

verification.check: An agent manifest can name its runtime and two runtimes are supported.

title: Specialist agents: domain research, controlled tools, Fabric task interfaces
statement: Specialist agents perform domain research, tool use and multimodal reasoning, interfacing through Fabric tasks/results, knowledge APIs and controlled tools.
rationale: Uncontrolled tool access lets an agent act outside its grant.

verification.check: An agent can invoke only tools in its explicit grant and its outputs are journaled.

title: Model Tournament scores by calibration, regime and information value
statement: A Model Tournament scores models by calibration, regime and information value against ForecastState and resolved outcomes.
rationale: The best of many models on one aggregate metric is selected by chance.

verification.check: Models are ranked per regime with calibration and information-value scores from resolved outcomes; a challenger that did not win its comparison cannot be promoted.

title: Forecast Market aggregates model votes via synthetic reputation
statement: A Forecast Market aggregates model votes using synthetic reputation/capital and emits ModelVote / ForecastConsensus.
rationale: Unweighted averaging gives a poor model the same voice as a proven one.

verification.check: Votes weighted by reputation produce a ForecastConsensus; equal weighting fails the test.

title: Adversarial/Verifier Society attacks leading forecasts
statement: An Adversarial/Verifier Society attacks leading forecasts and searches for contradictions, exchanging ChallengeRequest / VerificationResult.
rationale: A model asked whether a persuasive thesis holds usually agrees with it.

verification.check: A leading forecast receives challenges and a fatal challenge rejects it.

title: Curiosity ranks missing evidence by value of information
statement: Curiosity/Active Sensing ranks missing evidence by expected value of information and sends InformationRequests to the Scout Fabric.
rationale: Acquiring data by habit rather than by value wastes budget on what does not change decisions.

verification.check: Requests are ordered by computed value of information and reach the scout; random order fails.

title: Meta-Intelligence allocates attention, compute and model influence
statement: Meta-Intelligence allocates attention, compute and model influence, emitting ComputePlan / AgentBudget / ModelWeight.
rationale: Without explicit allocation, compute follows whatever asks loudest.

verification.check: A ComputePlan bounds per-agent budgets and model weights; exceeding a budget is refused.

title: world-branch-manager branches, reweights, prunes future-state trees
statement: A world-branch-manager branches, reweights and prunes future-state trees, storing compact WorldBranch records partitioned by scenario family.
rationale: Unpruned scenario trees grow without bound; unweighted ones give rare branches equal say.

verification.check: Branches carry weights summing to one and pruning keeps the tree within its bound.

title: market-digital-twin simulates exchange, venue, queue, participants, execution
statement: A market digital twin simulates exchange, venue, queue, participant and execution behaviour, run as sharded replay/simulation jobs.
rationale: Backtests without queue and participant modelling overstate fills.

verification.check: A replayed order receives queue-position-dependent fills; removing queue modelling changes fills and fails the test.

title: Macro/company twins simulate causal business and supply-chain dynamics
statement: Macro and company twins simulate causal business, macro and supply-chain dynamics with compact twin state and source manifests.
rationale: Without causal dynamics, second-order effects are invisible.

verification.check: A shock to an upstream entity propagates through the twin to dependants.

title: Rare-event factory generates adversarial combinations; only lessons persist
statement: A rare-event factory generates adversarial/unseen combinations; simulation outputs are ephemeral and only promoted lessons are retained.
rationale: History contains only the crises that happened; retaining every synthetic output is unbounded.

verification.check: Generated scenarios include moves outside history and only promoted lessons are persisted.

title: Counterfactual portfolio farm runs shadow hedges, timing and sizing
statement: A counterfactual portfolio farm runs shadow positions, alternate hedges, timing and sizing asynchronously and in parallel, storing compact packs.
rationale: A decision scored only against itself cannot show what it cost.

verification.check: Each decision has scored alternatives; removing the alternative scoring fails the test.

title: IBM Quantum reached only through a controlled asynchronous gateway
statement: IBM Quantum is reached only through a controlled, asynchronous quantum gateway.
rationale: Direct calls would put an external queue on a decision path and leak credentials widely.

verification.check: Only the gateway identity has egress to IBM hosts and the gateway queues jobs; a second caller fails the check.

title: Compute Intelligence Router learns best substrate per problem class
statement: A Compute Intelligence Router learns which substrate (CPU, GPU, TPU, quantum-inspired, QPU) gives the best verified result for each problem class.
rationale: Static routing keeps paying for substrates that never win.

verification.check: Recorded verified outcomes per problem class change the router's substrate choice.

title: CPU/Rust pools own deterministic compute as low-cost baseline
statement: CPU/Rust pools on Compute Engine own symbolic solvers, graph algorithms, deterministic services and Fabric/Reflex tooling, scaled by fixed reservations as the low-cost baseline.
rationale: Deterministic work on accelerators costs more and adds non-determinism.

verification.check: Execution nodes consume a specific reservation sized to target; deterministic services are Rust on CPU.

notes: GKE CPU pools named in text conflict with ADR 0024; Compute Engine half applies.

title: GPU substrate for training, multimodal inference, simulation
statement: GPU pools (Vertex custom training) serve foundation/specialist training, multimodal inference and simulation, with Spot for interruptible jobs.
rationale: Accelerator-shaped work on CPUs is slow and expensive.

verification.check: A training job spec names a GPU machine type and Spot for interruptible runs.

title: TPU7x substrate scheduled by compute router
statement: TPU7x (Ironwood) via Compute Engine serves large dense/MoE training, decode-heavy inference and high-scale simulation, scheduled by the compute router.
rationale: Placement for the largest training workloads.

verification.check: A TPU slice is reservable and the router can schedule onto it.

notes: JAX/PyTorch named: non-Rust.

title: Quantum-inspired classical baseline always available before any QPU claim
statement: Quantum-inspired classical heuristics (QUBO/Ising, annealing-style) are always available as the baseline before any QPU claim.
rationale: A QPU result compared to nothing proves nothing.

verification.check: SolverBenchmark always includes a classical solver record and refuses a candidate failing classical validation.

title: QPU work budgeted, off the hot path, classically verified
statement: QPU work runs in a budgeted queue, with no hot-path dependency and mandatory classical verification.
rationale: An unbudgeted QPU queue spends without bound; a hot-path dependency stalls execution.

verification.check: Jobs over budget are refused; no execution crate reaches a solver; every QPU result is validated classically.

title: capital-society-coordinator combines allocation, funding, liquidity, collateral proposals
statement: A capital-society-coordinator combines allocation, funding, liquidity and collateral proposals against the authoritative capital grants/ledger.
rationale: Independent proposers over-commit the same capital.

verification.check: Competing proposals are reconciled against the grant ledger and the sum never exceeds granted capital.

title: Survival kernel reserves cash, margin, liquidity, emergency buffers first
statement: A survival-kernel reserves cash, margin, liquidity and emergency buffers, under deterministic policy, before any capital is deployed.
rationale: Deploying capital before reserving buffers is how a book is forced to liquidate.

verification.check: Opportunity capital is released only after reserves in priority order; a book whose reserves exceed capital releases none. Reordering the waterfall fails the test.

title: hedge-brain searches multi-world hedge portfolios and unwind plans
statement: A hedge-brain searches multi-world hedge portfolios and unwind plans using the hybrid solver router, over positions and the forecast distribution.
rationale: Hedges sized to one forecast fail in the worlds it did not consider.

verification.check: A hedge plan is evaluated across scenario worlds and includes an unwind plan.

title: Confidence governor shrinks grants when calibration, OOD or disagreement deteriorates
statement: A model-risk/confidence-governor shrinks capital grants when calibration, out-of-distribution signals or model disagreement deteriorate.
rationale: A model that has stopped being right keeps its full allocation until a loss shows it.

verification.check: Worsening calibration reduces the grant; mutating the governor to ignore calibration fails the test.

title: shadow-portfolio-farm writes counterfactual sizing/hedge/timing outcome packs
statement: A shadow-portfolio-farm runs counterfactual sizing, hedge and timing portfolios as batch jobs writing compact outcome packs.
rationale: The realised choice is only meaningful scored against what it declined.

verification.check: Each allocation has shadow alternatives scored after resolution into a durable pack.

title: Spanner Graph holds promoted durable entities, never agent scratchpads
statement: Spanner Graph holds promoted durable entities, relationships, causal edges, world-model state and provenance references, and never agent scratchpads.
rationale: Scratchpads in the authoritative graph pollute truth with unvetted guesses.

verification.check: Only promoted entities can be written to the graph store; a scratchpad write is refused.

title: Bigtable holds high-rate ambient state, reputation, scores, features, branch indexes
statement: Bigtable holds high-rate ambient state, forecast reputation, model scores, live derived features and branch indexes.
rationale: High-rate state in a transactional store contends with the ledger.

verification.check: These record kinds are routed to the wide-column target and nothing else is.

title: BigQuery holds resolved outcomes, tournament history, research analytics
statement: BigQuery holds resolved forecast outcomes, tournament history, research analytics and large derived datasets.
rationale: Analytics in operational stores slow the operational path.

verification.check: Resolved outcomes are streamed to the warehouse.

title: Cloud Storage holds retained history, segments, artifacts; never raw-world corpus
statement: Cloud Storage holds retained tick/internal history, immutable Fabric segments, model artifacts and compact knowledge/world-state packs, and is never a general raw-world corpus.
rationale: An unbounded raw corpus is a cost and licensing liability.

verification.check: Archiver writes sealed segments and artifacts with deterministic names; writes outside the named classes are refused.

title: Agent memory is bounded and never authoritative truth
statement: Agent/session memory is bounded and is never authoritative financial or world truth.
rationale: Agent memory treated as truth lets a hallucination become a fact.

verification.check: Agent memory has a size bound and no decision path reads it as truth.

title: Public edge: Cloud DNS, global ALB, Cloud Armor, CDN, Certificate Manager
statement: The public edge is Cloud DNS plus a global external Application Load Balancer with Cloud Armor, Cloud CDN and Certificate Manager.
rationale: A public surface without WAF/DDoS and managed certificates is exposed by default.

sources.section: §12 Edge, Portal, API and Causal Action Plane

verification.check: A plan for an environment with a public edge creates the LB, security policy, CDN backend and certificate map.

title: Static content cached; dynamic BFF on Cloud Run behind serverless backends
statement: Static content is cached at the edge and the dynamic BFF runs on Cloud Run behind serverless backends.
rationale: Uncached static content loads the BFF; a BFF exposed directly bypasses the edge.

sources.section: §12 Edge, Portal, API and Causal Action Plane

verification.check: Every backend bucket is CDN-served and the BFF is a serverless NEG backend.

title: Customer identity on Identity Platform with strong MFA/passkeys
statement: Customer/application identities use Identity Platform with strong MFA/passkeys where supported.
rationale: Password-only customer accounts are taken over.

sources.section: §12 Edge, Portal, API and Causal Action Plane

verification.check: Identity Platform config has MFA mandatory (or enforced per tenant) and passkeys enabled.

title: Workforce/admin paths use Cloud Identity/IAM/IAP/PAM
statement: Internal workforce and admin paths use Cloud Identity, IAM, IAP and Privileged Access Manager.
rationale: Admin paths on public endpoints or standing privilege are the common breach route.

sources.section: §12 Edge, Portal, API and Causal Action Plane

verification.check: Every admin surface sits behind IAP and privileged roles are granted only via PAM entitlements.

title: Public API never exposes ledger tables, broker ports, Reflex nodes or keys
statement: The public API exposes portfolio/ledger-derived views and authorised commands only, never direct ledger tables, Fabric broker ports, Reflex nodes or custody keys.
rationale: Direct exposure of internal stores bypasses every control between them and the user.

sources.section: §12 Edge, Portal, API and Causal Action Plane

verification.check: The route table contains no route resolving to a ledger table, broker, node or key, and every mutating route raises a typed intent; adding such a route fails the suite.

title: Causal action adapters run as separate services per action class
statement: Causal action adapters (publication, outreach, product/pricing, market creation, operational tools) run as separate services.
rationale: One adapter process holding every action authority is one compromise away from all of them.

sources.section: §12 Edge, Portal, API and Causal Action Plane

verification.check: Each adapter class is its own deployable with its own identity.

title: Each action adapter carries identity, jurisdiction policy, rate limits, audit, stop
statement: Each causal action adapter has an action identity, jurisdiction/channel policy, rate limits, immutable audit and rollback/stop controls.
rationale: An action without identity, limits and a stop control cannot be attributed or halted.

sources.section: §12 Edge, Portal, API and Causal Action Plane

verification.check: A tool missing any of these declarations cannot be constructed; deleting one field check fails the test.

title: Crawler/scout isolated in dedicated project/VPC/pools and egress identity
statement: Crawler/scout workloads run in a dedicated project/VPC/node pools with their own egress identity.
rationale: Untrusted fetching in the trading network gives web content a path to trading systems.

sources.section: §12 Edge, Portal, API and Causal Action Plane

verification.check: Scouts have their own identity and network and only they hold information-source egress.

title: Untrusted web content cannot invoke high-authority tools or production secrets
statement: Untrusted web content cannot directly invoke high-authority tools or reach production secrets.
rationale: Prompt injection via fetched content is the obvious route to tool misuse.

sources.section: §12 Edge, Portal, API and Causal Action Plane

verification.check: Ingested content has no code path to tool invocation or secret reads.

title: Autonomous development never bypasses Git, test, attestation or deploy policy
statement: Agent-produced code and infrastructure changes go through Git, tests, attestation and deployment policy like any other change.
rationale: An agent with a side door to production makes every control optional.

verification.check: Deploy requires a passing CI run on a repository commit and signs only that; a fork/PR commit cannot be signed.

title: Planner agent cannot merge or deploy
statement: The planner agent role may read and plan but cannot merge or deploy.
rationale: Section 13's role table makes this the hard boundary for the role.

verification.check: The boundary is enforced by credentials/config or a gate, and a run attempting the forbidden action is refused.

title: Coder agent has sandboxed credentials, no prod secrets
statement: The coder agent works with sandboxed credentials and never holds production secrets.
rationale: Section 13's role table makes this the hard boundary for the role.

verification.check: The boundary is enforced by credentials/config or a gate, and a run attempting the forbidden action is refused.

title: Test agent cannot waive failing risk or performance gates
statement: The test/replay agent cannot waive a failing risk or performance gate.
rationale: Section 13's role table makes this the hard boundary for the role.

verification.check: The boundary is enforced by credentials/config or a gate, and a run attempting the forbidden action is refused.

title: Security findings severity controls promotion
statement: Security-agent findings are triaged by a severity policy that controls promotion.
rationale: Section 13's role table makes this the hard boundary for the role.

verification.check: The boundary is enforced by credentials/config or a gate, and a run attempting the forbidden action is refused.

title: Architecture agent cannot silently redefine non-negotiables
statement: Architecture checks enforce dependency rules, hot-path violations and state ownership, and non-negotiables cannot be redefined silently.
rationale: Section 13's role table makes this the hard boundary for the role.

verification.check: The boundary is enforced by credentials/config or a gate, and a run attempting the forbidden action is refused.

title: Reviewer independent of coder by model and context
statement: The reviewer agent uses a separate model/context from the primary coder.
rationale: Section 13's role table makes this the hard boundary for the role.

verification.check: The boundary is enforced by credentials/config or a gate, and a run attempting the forbidden action is refused.

title: Release agent promotes by immutable digest; no direct kubectl/SSH
statement: The release agent updates environment desired state by immutable digest after gates and has no direct kubectl/SSH to production.
rationale: Section 13's role table makes this the hard boundary for the role.

verification.check: The boundary is enforced by credentials/config or a gate, and a run attempting the forbidden action is refused.

title: SRE auto-remediation limited to signed runbooks and approved actions
statement: SRE agent auto-remediation is limited to signed runbooks and approved actions.
rationale: Section 13's role table makes this the hard boundary for the role.

verification.check: The boundary is enforced by credentials/config or a gate, and a run attempting the forbidden action is refused.

title: Learning agent proposals still pass promotion gates
statement: The learning agent may propose capability changes from incidents/reviews/benchmarks, but promotion stays gated.
rationale: Section 13's role table makes this the hard boundary for the role.

verification.check: The boundary is enforced by credentials/config or a gate, and a run attempting the forbidden action is refused.

title: Agent workers are ephemeral with scoped service accounts
statement: Agent orchestration runs on a management plane and execution workers are ephemeral jobs/build workers with scoped service accounts.
rationale: Long-lived agent workers accumulate credentials and state.

verification.check: Each agent task runs in an ephemeral worker under a task-scoped identity.

title: Agent sandboxes: ephemeral, egress-limited, quota, read-only telemetry, synthetic data
statement: Agent sandboxes are ephemeral namespaces/projects with egress policy, quota, read-only production telemetry by default and synthetic/test data when possible.
rationale: An agent sandbox with write access to production telemetry or real data is not a sandbox.

verification.check: A sandbox identity has only read on telemetry and no data-store grants.

title: One policy-enforcing, audited model gateway for agents
statement: Agents use approved models only through one policy-enforcing gateway; credentials stay in Secret Manager and requests are audited.
rationale: Per-agent model credentials sprawl and requests go unaudited.

verification.check: Every agent model request passes the gateway, which records it; a direct call fails.

title: Architecture memory indexed for agents
statement: ADRs, contracts, service catalogue, SLOs, runbooks and the blueprint are indexed for agents.
rationale: Agents that cannot find the rules re-derive them wrongly.

verification.check: The index lists every ADR, blueprint source with hash, the deployable binaries, and runbooks; a missing entry fails.

title: Agents cite the rule they change when proposing an exception
statement: An agent proposing an exception must cite the rule it is changing.
rationale: Silent exceptions erode rules without anyone deciding to.

verification.check: A PR template field naming the rule is required and checked.

title: No invisible changes: repairs become commits/PRs or audited runtime actions
statement: Any autonomous repair that changes code/config becomes a normal Git commit/PR, or a pre-approved runtime action whose event is durably audited.
rationale: An unrecorded fix is an unreviewable change.

verification.check: A remediation produces an audit record before the effect; an effect without a record fails.

title: Agent work isolated in branches/worktrees with deterministic acceptance and budgets
statement: Agent work is decomposed into isolated branches/worktrees with deterministic acceptance criteria and budgeted tool/model usage.
rationale: Unbudgeted parallel agents spend without bound and collide.

verification.check: Each task carries acceptance criteria and a budget that is enforced.

title: Orchestrator keeps dependency DAGs and prevents overlapping edits
statement: An agent orchestrator maintains dependency DAGs and prevents multiple agents editing the same ownership boundary without merge coordination.
rationale: Parallel agents editing the same files or allocating the same IDs collide.

verification.check: Two tasks claiming the same boundary are serialised.

title: Agent sandboxes have no production credentials
statement: Ephemeral agent sandboxes (Cloud Run Jobs, GKE Jobs or build workers) never have production credentials available.
rationale: A sandbox holding prod credentials makes agent compromise a production compromise.

verification.check: No production-scoped grant exists for any sandbox identity.

title: Agent changes carry machine-checkable evidence
statement: Every agent-produced change generates machine-checkable evidence: tests, replay deltas, benchmark deltas, security results and architecture-contract checks.
rationale: A change justified by prose cannot be checked.

verification.check: CI emits each evidence class as an artifact for every PR.

title: Terraform/GitOps is the only normal path to persistent cloud state
statement: Agents may propose services/models/tools, but Terraform/GitOps remains the only normal path to persistent cloud state.
rationale: Console changes drift from the reviewed state.

verification.check: infra apply consumes a saved plan; drift detectors raise findings.

title: SRE agents turn regressions into replay/fuzz/game-day tests first
statement: SRE agents learn from incidents and turn each regression into a replay/fuzz/game-day test before proposing a fix.
rationale: A fix without a regression test lets the incident recur.

verification.check: Each incident record links a new test that fails before the fix.

title: Repository algorik-app owns its declared scope
statement: A repository named algorik-app owns: Rust services, Reflex, Fabric, APIs, shared crates, tests.
rationale: Separating ownership by repository bounds blast radius and review scope.

verification.check: The algorik-app repository exists and holds exactly that scope.

notes: Conflicts with the platform's one-repository rule.

title: Repository algorik-models owns its declared scope
statement: A repository named algorik-models owns: training code, evaluation, feature definitions, distillation, model manifests.
rationale: Separating ownership by repository bounds blast radius and review scope.

verification.check: The algorik-models repository exists and holds exactly that scope.

notes: Conflicts with the platform's one-repository rule.

title: Repository algorik-infra owns its declared scope
statement: A repository named algorik-infra owns: Terraform modules/stacks for org/projects/network/GKE/Spanner/data/build/security.
rationale: Separating ownership by repository bounds blast radius and review scope.

verification.check: The algorik-infra repository exists and holds exactly that scope.

notes: Conflicts with the platform's one-repository rule.

title: Repository algorik-platform-config owns its declared scope
statement: A repository named algorik-platform-config owns: Config Sync cluster baseline, policies, CRDs, observability agents, GitOps controllers.
rationale: Separating ownership by repository bounds blast radius and review scope.

verification.check: The algorik-platform-config repository exists and holds exactly that scope.

notes: Conflicts with the platform's one-repository rule.

title: Repository algorik-env owns its declared scope
statement: A repository named algorik-env owns: environment desired state: application/model/policy digests and per-region rollout declarations.
rationale: Separating ownership by repository bounds blast radius and review scope.

verification.check: The algorik-env repository exists and holds exactly that scope.

notes: Conflicts with the platform's one-repository rule.

title: Repository algorik-schemas owns its declared scope
statement: A repository named algorik-schemas owns: Fabric event schemas, compatibility rules, generated Rust clients/types, data contracts.
rationale: Separating ownership by repository bounds blast radius and review scope.

verification.check: The algorik-schemas repository exists and holds exactly that scope.

notes: Conflicts with the platform's one-repository rule.

title: Repository algorik-runbooks owns its declared scope
statement: A repository named algorik-runbooks owns: SRE runbooks, game-day definitions, remediation policy, architecture acceptance tests.
rationale: Separating ownership by repository bounds blast radius and review scope.

verification.check: The algorik-runbooks repository exists and holds exactly that scope.

notes: Conflicts with the platform's one-repository rule.

title: Branch protection requires tests and risk-scaled independent review
statement: Branch protections require tests and independent review scaled by risk class for every PR, whether from a human or an authorised agent.
rationale: Unreviewed changes to safety paths reach main.

verification.check: Main refuses a merge without passing checks and a code-owner review.

title: CI uses WIF short-lived credentials; no stored service-account keys
statement: GitHub Actions exchanges OIDC for short-lived GCP credentials through Workload Identity Federation, and no service-account key is stored anywhere.
rationale: A stored key is a permanent credential that outlives every rotation.

verification.check: No google_service_account_key in Terraform, org policy disables key creation/upload, and workflows authenticate via the WIF provider.

title: Builds run in a Cloud Build private pool, reproducibly
statement: Builds run in a Cloud Build private pool inside private networking and are reproducible.
rationale: A non-reproducible build cannot be verified against its source; public runners see build secrets.

verification.check: Two builds of the same commit yield the same digest; builds run in a private pool.

title: Rust builds use locked dependencies
statement: Rust builds use locked dependencies.
rationale: An unlocked build resolves a different dependency graph from the one reviewed.

verification.check: Every cargo build in CI and the Dockerfile passes --locked.

title: cargo-deny and cargo-audit gate CI
statement: CI runs cargo-deny and cargo-audit as gates.
rationale: Known-vulnerable or disallowed crates reach a build.

verification.check: The audit and deny jobs fail the workflow on findings.

title: Clippy and unit/property tests gate CI
statement: CI runs clippy and unit/property tests as gates.
rationale: Lint and test failures ship.

verification.check: clippy and cargo test --no-fail-fast run on every PR.

title: Fuzz tests gate CI
statement: CI runs fuzz tests as a gate.
rationale: Parsers fail on inputs nobody wrote by hand.

verification.check: A fuzz job runs on PRs and fails on a crash.

title: Replay and benchmark gates in CI
statement: CI runs replay and benchmark gates.
rationale: Behavioural and performance regressions ship silently.

verification.check: A replay comparison and a benchmark threshold fail the build on regression.

title: Terraform plan before artifacts accepted
statement: A Terraform plan runs before artifacts are accepted.
rationale: Infrastructure that cannot plan is discovered at apply.

verification.check: A plan job runs on PRs touching infrastructure.

title: Kubernetes policy checks before artifacts accepted
statement: Kubernetes manifests pass policy checks before artifacts are accepted.
rationale: A manifest that relaxes a control reaches the cluster.

verification.check: Rendered manifests are checked for the invariants.

title: Secret scan, SAST, SCA and container scan before acceptance
statement: Secret scan, SAST/SCA and container scan run before artifacts are accepted.
rationale: Leaked secrets and known vulnerabilities ship.

verification.check: Each scanner runs and blocks.

title: Architecture rule tests before acceptance
statement: Architecture rule tests run before artifacts are accepted.
rationale: Boundary violations ship.

verification.check: The architecture suite runs in CI's cargo test and deploy gates on CI.

title: Artifact Registry stores images, Rust packages, OCI bundles by immutable digest
statement: Artifact Registry stores images, Rust packages and OCI deployment bundles by immutable digest.
rationale: A mutable tag lets whoever can push change what deploys.

verification.check: Repositories have immutable tags and deploys reference digests.

title: SBOM, provenance and scan results attached to artifacts
statement: SBOM, provenance and scan results are attached to each stored artifact.
rationale: An artifact without provenance cannot be traced to source.

verification.check: The registry entry for an image has SBOM and provenance attestations.

title: KMS/HSM signs release, model and policy manifests
statement: Cloud KMS/HSM signs release, model and policy manifests.
rationale: Symmetric or reproducible signing keys let anyone who can compute them forge policy.

verification.check: Each manifest signature verifies with a KMS public key; a manifest signed with any other key is refused.

title: Binary Authorization requires trusted attestations at deploy
statement: Binary Authorization and admission policy require trusted attestations for deployed workloads.
rationale: Unattested images run.

verification.check: Default rule is REQUIRE_ATTESTATION with ENFORCED_BLOCK_AND_AUDIT_LOG naming the attestor.

notes: Text says GKE workloads; here applied to Cloud Run.

title: Desired state updated by digest; Config Sync and Argo CD reconcile
statement: The release agent updates the environment desired state with exact digests; Config Sync reconciles the platform baseline and Argo CD reconciles application state.
rationale: Imperative deploys leave no reviewed desired state.

verification.check: A promotion is a commit of digests and reconciliation follows it.

title: Same immutable artifact promoted dev→integration→replay→paper→staging→prod
statement: Kargo promotes the same immutable artifact through dev, integration, replay, paper, staging and prod regions; rebuilding per environment is prohibited.
rationale: A per-environment rebuild means prod runs bytes nobody tested.

verification.check: The digest promoted to each stage equals the digest built once; a second build fails the check.

title: Argo Rollouts canary/blue-green for GKE services
statement: GKE services roll out by canary/blue-green via Argo Rollouts.
rationale: All-at-once rollouts make every regression a full outage.

verification.check: Rollout objects define steps and analysis.

title: Reflex/Fabric use drain/stage/epoch activation, not pod canaries
statement: Reflex and Fabric components roll out via component-specific drain/stage/epoch activation rather than generic pod canaries.
rationale: A pod canary on a stateful venue session double-sends or drops orders.

verification.check: A new incarnation fences the old one by epoch before activating.

title: Rollout SLOs enforced; regression auto-rolls back and opens incident
statement: Monitoring/replay comparators enforce rollout SLOs; a regression rolls back automatically and creates an incident/task.
rationale: A regression nobody notices stays deployed.

verification.check: A spent error budget blocks release and a regression triggers rollback.

title: GKE services canary with SLO gate and instant previous-digest rollback
statement: GKE services deploy via Argo CD + Kargo + Argo Rollouts with canary by traffic/replicas, an SLO gate, and instant rollback to the previous digest.
rationale: Slow rollback extends incidents.

verification.check: Rollback to the previous digest is one action.

title: Reflex rollout: standby, replay shadow, drain/fence, activate epoch, compare, expand
statement: Reflex binaries roll out as immutable VM images: standby first, replay shadow, drain/fence, activate epoch, compare, expand.
rationale: Replacing the active node in place loses the venue session.

verification.check: A rollout drill follows the sequence and the old node is fenced before activation.

title: Fabric broker rollout: drain leaders, verify RF, replace one broker, rejoin
statement: Fabric brokers roll out by draining leaders/partitions, verifying replication factor, replacing one broker, rejoining, and repeating.
rationale: Replacing brokers without verified replication loses quorum-acked records.

verification.check: A rolling replacement preserves every quorum-acked record.

title: Model/policy rollout: shadow, paper/replay, stage, atomic epoch activation, rollback retained
statement: Models/policy roll out as signed OCI manifests with GCS weights: shadow score, paper/replay, stage locally, atomic epoch activation, with rollback retained.
rationale: A model activated without shadow evidence is an untested change to decisions.

verification.check: Promotion requires shadow evidence, activation is atomic by sequence, and rollback restores the parent.

title: Terraform: gated apply, plan artifact, change windows for core resources
statement: Terraform changes go through plan plus gated apply; folder/project/network/database changes have explicit change windows and a plan artifact.
rationale: Unplanned applies to core resources cause outages.

verification.check: Apply consumes the saved plan artifact; core changes are refused outside a window.

title: Schema changes: compatibility gate, additive first, dual read/write, retire after inventory
statement: Schemas live in a registry with a CI compatibility gate; changes are additive first with dual-read/write migrations, and a field is retired only after a consumer inventory proves it safe.
rationale: A breaking schema change strands consumers.

verification.check: Removing a field fails the gate; adding passes.

title: Least-privilege, group-based IAM
statement: Human and workload identity uses Cloud Identity/IAM with least privilege and group-based access.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: Privileged Access Manager time-bounded elevation
statement: Sensitive operations use Privileged Access Manager for time-bounded elevation with approvals.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: External CI uses Workload Identity Federation
statement: GitHub/external CI obtains short-lived GCP access through Workload Identity Federation without service-account keys.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: Workload Identity for GKE pods; no node-wide credentials
statement: GKE pods map to GCP service identities with no node-wide credentials.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: Secret Manager with rotation, versioning, audit
statement: Venue/API credentials and non-key secrets live in Secret Manager with rotation, versioning and audit, delivered as files.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: KMS/HSM for CMEK, signing, attestation roots
statement: Cloud KMS/HSM provides CMEK, package signing, high-assurance key material and attestation roots.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: Certificate Authority Service mTLS for Fabric/VM identities
statement: Certificate Authority Service issues mTLS certificates for Fabric/VM and internal workload identities outside a mesh.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: VPC Service Controls perimeters around ledger/data/AI
statement: VPC Service Controls perimeters surround ledger, data and AI projects.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: Cloud Armor WAF/DDoS/rate controls internet-facing
statement: Every internet-facing surface has Cloud Armor WAF, DDoS (adaptive protection) and rate controls.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: Hierarchical firewall / NGFW egress segmentation
statement: Organisation/folder hierarchical firewall policies (Cloud NGFW) provide network policy, egress segmentation and narrow lateral paths.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: Security Command Center posture and findings
statement: Security Command Center aggregates posture, findings and threats with response integration.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: Artifact Analysis and Binary Authorization
statement: Artifact Analysis scans images and Binary Authorization enforces at deploy time.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: Sensitive Data Protection for PII in lake/analytics
statement: Sensitive Data Protection discovers, classifies and redacts PII/sensitive data in lake/analytics.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: Cloud Audit Logs and Asset Inventory
statement: Cloud Audit Logs and Cloud Asset Inventory provide administrative/data-access evidence and change visibility.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: IAP for internal/admin web; no public management endpoints
statement: Internal/admin web access uses IAP and no management endpoint is public.
rationale: Section 15 control table.

verification.check: The control exists in Terraform and is asserted by a test or plan.

title: Custody, deploy-signing, Fabric identity and user-auth keys are separate trust domains
statement: Custody/transfer keys, deployment-signing keys, Fabric identity keys and user-auth keys are separate trust domains.
rationale: A shared key domain lets one compromise cross into another.

verification.check: Each key class is a distinct KMS key with disjoint IAM.

title: Engineering-agent compromise cannot yield capital-moving authority
statement: Compromise of an engineering agent must not yield authority to move capital.
rationale: Agent compromise becoming a funds-movement compromise.

verification.check: No CI/agent identity holds any treasury/withdrawal grant.

title: Trading-service compromise cannot yield deployment-signing authority
statement: Compromise of a trading service must not yield deployment-signing authority.
rationale: A compromised workload signing its own replacement.

verification.check: No workload identity holds signer rights on the attestor key.

title: OpenTelemetry instrumentation everywhere
statement: Every process is instrumented with OpenTelemetry (SDK/collector).
rationale: Uninstrumented processes cannot be operated.

verification.check: Each binary exports OTLP; a binary without an exporter fails the check.

notes: An OTel SDK crate would breach ADR 0002; OTLP/JSON is produced in-tree.

title: Reflex/Fabric export asynchronously to regional collectors
statement: Reflex and Fabric export telemetry asynchronously to regional collectors.
rationale: Synchronous export puts the collector on the order path.

verification.check: Export happens off the pass thread to a regional collector.

title: No logging call may block order processing
statement: No logging call may block order processing.
rationale: A slow log sink stalls the order path.

verification.check: Logging on the pass path is sampled/non-blocking; an injected slow sink does not delay a pass.

rationale: Metrics nothing collects page nobody.

verification.check: A collector scrapes each service and alert policies evaluate.

title: High-rate logs strictly sampled; raw history in Fabric/GCS not logs
statement: Application/control logs go to Cloud Logging with strict sampling on high-rate paths; raw tick/decision history belongs in Fabric/GCS, not log ingestion.
rationale: Per-event logging makes log cost proportional to traffic.

verification.check: High-rate paths log through the sampler and carry dropped counts.

title: Traces for warm/API; correlation IDs bridge into Reflex/Fabric metadata
statement: Cloud Trace covers warm/API workflows, and sampled correlation IDs bridge into Reflex/Fabric event metadata without distributed-trace network calls on the hot path.
rationale: Without correlation, an operator cannot follow a decision from API to cell.

verification.check: A correlation id set at the API appears in the cell's event metadata.

title: Network telemetry: flow logs, connectivity tests, LB and Interconnect metrics
statement: Network observability uses VPC Flow Logs where appropriate, Connectivity Tests, load-balancer telemetry and Interconnect/VPN metrics.
rationale: Network faults are invisible without flow data.

verification.check: Subnets on trading/zone paths carry flow logs.

title: SLOs per plane with error budgets driving release policy
statement: SLOs are declared per plane and dependency, with error budgets that drive release policy.
rationale: SLOs that do not gate releases are decoration.

verification.check: A spent budget refuses a release for that plane only.

title: Fabric backlog and ledger reconciliation are product SLOs
statement: Fabric backlog and ledger reconciliation are product SLOs, not only infrastructure metrics.
rationale: Treating them as infrastructure hides product failure.

verification.check: Both appear as declared SLOs with targets.

title: AIOps SRE agent diagnoses and executes pre-approved actions with audit
statement: An SRE agent reads telemetry, compares runbooks and recent diffs, opens incidents/PRs, scales permitted services and executes pre-approved rollback/restart/drain actions with audit.
rationale: Manual diagnosis is slow; unaudited automation is dangerous.

verification.check: A detected anomaly yields an incident and only a runbook action, audited.

rationale: Per-component SLOs are what release and paging decisions are made on.

title: Reflex standby stays fenced; failure loses only that shard's venue session
statement: On a Reflex process/VM failure the standby stays fenced until failover criteria are met and only that shard's venue connection is lost.
rationale: An unfenced standby double-sends; a shared session loses every shard.

verification.check: Killing the primary does not activate the standby until criteria pass; other shards keep sessions.

title: Reflex recovery after liveness, fencing, venue-session checks; no zero-gap promise
statement: Reflex recovers by restart or standby promotion only after liveness, fencing and venue-session checks; recovery targets are measured per venue and zero-gap failover is not promised.
rationale: Promoting before the old session is dead produces duplicate orders.

verification.check: A drill records per-venue recovery time and the promotion follows the three checks.

title: Zone loss: Fabric RF3 retains quorum; Reflex promotes standby
statement: On loss of one zone, Fabric RF3 and the regional control plane retain quorum and Reflex can promote its standby.
rationale: A single-zone deployment loses everything with the zone.

verification.check: Zone-loss drill keeps quorum-acked records and promotes the standby.

title: Broker failure: leader moves, producers refresh, quorum-acked records preserved
statement: On a Fabric broker failure the partition leader moves to a follower, producers refresh the map, and quorum-acked records are preserved before the broker is replaced and rebalanced.
rationale: Losing an acknowledged record breaks the audit trail.

verification.check: Killing a broker loses no acked record.

title: Fabric region loss: Reflex continues on cached policy; mirrored topics elsewhere
statement: On loss of a whole Fabric region, Reflex continues under cached policy, critical mirrored topics remain available elsewhere, and the region is rebuilt from replicas/GCS archives.
rationale: A region outage must not stop other regions or the region's own execution.

verification.check: With the broker unreachable the cell passes on its last verified policy; spool pressure halts only per the journal wire.

title: Regional control-plane loss: Reflex continues; rebuild from Terraform and GitOps
statement: On regional GKE (control plane) loss, Reflex and Fabric journaling continue, other regions take research/control work, and the cluster is rebuilt from Terraform + Config Sync + Argo.
rationale: Control-plane loss must not become an execution outage.

verification.check: Deleting the control plane leaves cells passing; terraform + argo rebuilds it.

title: Global cognition loss: no new models; trading follows degradation envelope
statement: On loss of global cognition/AI, no new models or research are produced and local trading follows its freshness/degradation envelope with no hot-path impact.
rationale: Cognition on the hot path turns an AI outage into a trading outage.

verification.check: With every centre-fed capability stale, the cell's sizing multiplier falls per the table and passes continue.

title: Spanner leader move: monitor outcome-to-ledger backlog
statement: When the Spanner leader region moves, the ledger tolerates latency change and the outcome-to-ledger backlog is monitored.
rationale: A silently growing backlog means outcomes are unrecorded.

verification.check: The backlog gauge is recorded and alerted.

title: Bigtable failover via multi-cluster routing and app profiles
statement: Bigtable uses multi-cluster routed reads for failover, app profiles define behaviour, and single-cluster transactional workloads fail over explicitly with replay from Fabric/GCS.
rationale: A single cluster is a single point of failure.

verification.check: Instance has ≥2 clusters and app profiles.

title: GCS research data per residency; derived stores rehydrated from immutable objects
statement: GCS uses replicated/dual-region locations per residency policy, regional landing is the source segment until archived, and derived stores can be rehydrated from immutable objects.
rationale: Derived stores that cannot be rebuilt are a second, unverifiable truth.

verification.check: A derived store rebuilt from archived segments equals the original.

title: GitOps plane loss: workloads keep running; recreate from Git
statement: On GitOps management-plane loss, running workloads continue, reconciliation pauses, and the plane is recreated from Git.
rationale: A control plane that workloads depend on is a hidden SPOF.

verification.check: Stopping Argo leaves services serving.

title: Registry region loss: nodes keep local images; secondary repository before prod
statement: On Artifact Registry region loss existing nodes keep local images and rollout pauses; release artifacts are replicated to a designated secondary repository before prod promotion.
rationale: A single registry region blocks every recovery deploy.

verification.check: A secondary repository exists and promotion to prod checks the artifact is there.

title: Autonomous dev plane is never an availability dependency
statement: If the autonomous development plane is lost, no autonomous changes happen, production keeps running, and the human/manual pipeline remains available.
rationale: Agents must be a convenience, not a dependency.

verification.check: Every deploy/infra workflow is human-dispatchable and no runtime component calls an agent service.

title: No reactive autoscale of Reflex during a market burst
statement: Reflex is never reactively autoscaled during a market burst.
rationale: An autoscaler that adds a second instance creates two venue sessions.

verification.check: No autoscaler resource targets the execution-node group; adding one fails the suite.

title: Reflex scales by sharding sessions/instruments and pre-provisioning
statement: Reflex scales intentionally by sharding venue sessions/instruments across VMs and pre-provisioning capacity.
rationale: Unsharded growth overloads one node.

verification.check: Nodes are declared per shard with reservations.

title: Mesh exchanges compressed state with bounded fan-out and message size
statement: The Reflex Mesh exchanges compressed state only, bounds fan-out and message sizes, and never broadcasts raw tick streams globally.
rationale: Global raw broadcast saturates links and leaks venue data.

verification.check: Over-size frames and over-fan-out updates are refused, not truncated.

title: Fabric scales by brokers and partitions with zone-loss headroom
statement: The Fabric scales by adding brokers, moving leaders/followers and increasing partitions by domain, keeping headroom for zone loss and maintenance.
rationale: A Fabric that cannot add brokers caps platform throughput.

verification.check: Broker count and partitions are configurable with headroom.

title: GKE services autoscale via HPA/VPA, lag metrics, Cluster Autoscaler
statement: GKE services scale with HPA/VPA on custom lag/queue metrics and Cluster Autoscaler for warm/batch workloads.
rationale: Fixed capacity either wastes or saturates.

verification.check: HPA objects exist.

title: Bigtable autoscaling with hotspot-safe row keys and per-workload app profiles
statement: Bigtable uses managed autoscaling, hotspot-safe row keys and workload-specific app profiles.
rationale: Hotspotted keys defeat autoscaling.

verification.check: Autoscaling config, row-key design tests and app profiles exist.

title: Spanner autoscaling with high floor; schema eliminates hotspots
statement: Spanner uses managed autoscaling with a high floor, and schema/key design eliminates hotspots before scaling.
rationale: Hotspots make added capacity useless.

verification.check: Autoscaling config with min ≥ floor.

title: BigQuery separate research, backtest and BI reservations
statement: BigQuery uses separate research, backtest and BI reservations/workload management so no one job monopolises compute.
rationale: One runaway query starves every other workload.

verification.check: Three reservations and assignments exist.

title: GCS partitioned, immutable, reasonably sized segments; tiny objects compacted async
statement: GCS objects are partitioned by source/date/instrument, written as immutable reasonably sized segments, and tiny objects are compacted asynchronously.
rationale: Millions of tiny objects make listing and replay slow and costly.

verification.check: Archive names partition by source/date and compaction merges small objects off the write path.

title: AI training queue/quota-aware, Spot where safe, reserved capacity if justified
statement: AI training uses queue- and quota-aware scheduling, Spot where interruption is safe, and fixed reserved capacity for critical retraining only if justified.
rationale: Unscheduled training exhausts quota and budget.

verification.check: Job specs carry Spot/queue settings.

title: Autonomous-dev workers scale independently with concurrency quotas
statement: Autonomous-dev ephemeral workers and build pools scale independently, with concurrency quotas protecting source APIs and budgets.
rationale: Unbounded agent concurrency exhausts API quotas and spend.

verification.check: Worker pools have max concurrency.
